newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CVRD's auction price too high for Valecom group.
newsitem.headline: CVRD's auction price too high for Valecom group.

text.p: The 32.00 reais a share paid by the winning Valepar consortium for Brazil's Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) Tuesday was the maximum the rival Valecom group was willing to go, a Valecom group advisor said.
"The consortium had agreed before the auction that 32.00 reais was the maximum it would pay for CVRD," said Paulo Ferraz, president of private bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen.
Bozano, Simonsen represented the Valecom group in the auction and was advising South Africa's Anglo-American, one of the leaders of the consortium with Brazil's Grupo Votorantim.
Ferraz said the decision to drop out of the running when the last bid reached 32.00 reais was taken by all members of the consortium and not only by the Japanese investors who were part of the group.
Newspapers today said the Japanese gave the final word on Valecom's move to drop out of the auction.
Valecom's next bid should have been of 32.20 reais after Valepar, led by Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN, made the final winning offer of 32.00 reais per share for a 41.7 percent stake of CVRD.

"We knew how far we could go. Our next bid would have been of 32.20 reais, but we were not alone. We had to obey," the leader of the Valecom group, Votorantim president Antonio Ermirio de Moraes, was quoted as saying by O Globo newspaper.
Ferraz recognized that the successive delays in the CVRD auction due to a number of court injunctions blocking the sale were worrisome.
"Everybody was getting tired. It was obviously a marathon. An entire week without a minute to rest," he said.
Despite the delays, Ferraz thinks the government made no mistakes regarding the legal challenges. He noted that all lawsuits against CVRD's sell-off were ideologically motivated.
"The people behind the lawsuits were the same people who oppose every privatization," he said.
